Description: Default to written async communication. Reserve sync (meetings) for brainstorming and sensitive conversations only. Async = respects deep work + time zones.
Why_It_Matters: Remote teams in different time zones can't rely on meetings. Async forces clear thinking and creates documentation automatically.
Do_This: Write proposals before meetings|Use Loom for walkthroughs (3-5 min)|Thread everything in Slack|Set response expectations (SLA: 24 hrs for non-urgent)
Avoid_This: Real-time everything|@channel for non-urgent|Expecting immediate responses|Meeting for every decision

Description: Document ALL team processes in one place: communication norms, decision-making, working hours, tools, rituals. New hire's first read.
Why_It_Matters: Reduces onboarding time from weeks to days. Eliminates 'ask someone' culture. Creates consistency as team grows.
Do_This: Cover: tools, communication norms, meeting cadence, decision process, escalation, time off policy|Update quarterly|Make it searchable
Avoid_This: Tribal knowledge ('just ask Sarah')|Outdated handbook|Too long (keep actionable)|No ownership (assign maintainer)

Description: Set 3-4 hours of overlap when everyone should be available for sync communication. Outside overlap = async only. Respect boundaries.
Why_It_Matters: Enables global hiring while maintaining team cohesion. Clear expectations reduce frustration and guilt about offline time.
Do_This: Pick 3-4 hour window that works for most|Document in How We Work|All meetings within overlap|Protect deep work outside overlap
Avoid_This: Expecting same-timezone behavior|Meetings outside overlap|No clear boundaries|Punishing people for being offline

Description: If it's not written down it doesn't exist. Every decision, process, and piece of knowledge must be documented and findable.
Why_It_Matters: Remote teams can't tap colleagues on the shoulder. Documentation IS the communication backbone. Also reduces bus factor.
Do_This: Document decisions WITH reasoning|Use templates for recurring docs|Link related docs|Assign doc owners|Monthly doc review
Avoid_This: 'We'll remember'|Outdated docs (worse than no docs)|Too many tools (single source of truth)|No search functionality

Description: Intentional culture-building since accidental hallway conversations don't happen. Weekly social + monthly team event + quarterly deep connection.
Why_It_Matters: Without intentional effort remote teams become transactional. Isolation → disengagement → quit. Culture requires active investment.
Do_This: Weekly informal chat (15 min, optional)|Monthly virtual team activity|Quarterly virtual offsite|Donut pairings for random 1:1s|Celebrate wins publicly in Slack
Avoid_This: Mandatory fun|Too many social events|No budget for team events|Ignoring introverts' preferences

Description: Measure output and results not hours online. Trust by default. Green dot on Slack ≠ productivity.
Why_It_Matters: Activity monitoring destroys trust. Results-based management attracts top talent who value autonomy.
Do_This: Set clear weekly deliverables|Weekly async check-in (what I did / what I'll do / blockers)|Monthly 1:1 for growth|Quarterly OKR review
Avoid_This: Monitoring screen time|Green dot culture|Micromanaging daily tasks|No clear deliverables

Description: Remote hiring requires different process: async-first screening, take-home over whiteboard, timezone-compatible stages, paid trial period.
Why_It_Matters: Access 10x larger talent pool. But remote interviews need different skills — harder to read culture fit virtually.
Do_This: Async video screening (Loom)|Take-home relevant to actual work (max 4 hrs)|Paid 2-week trial project|Culture interview with team|Strong reference checks
Avoid_This: Whiteboard coding|All-day interview marathon|Not testing async communication skills|Hiring without trial period

Description: Invest in team's workspace: stipend for desk/chair/monitor. Proper setup = better output + fewer health issues. $500-$1500 one-time.
Why_It_Matters: Ergonomic issues cause long-term health problems and reduce productivity. Small investment with massive ROI.
Do_This: $1000-$1500 home office stipend|Required: external monitor + ergonomic chair|Good microphone (not laptop mic)|Proper lighting for video calls
Avoid_This: Expecting people to work from couch|No equipment budget|Poor audio quality on calls|Ignoring RSI risks

Description: Make decisions without meetings using RFC (Request for Comments) or Advice Process. Write proposal → collect feedback async → decide with deadline.
Why_It_Matters: Meetings are the most expensive way to make decisions. Async decisions are better documented and more inclusive (introverts participate equally).
Do_This: Write proposal with context + options + recommendation|Set feedback deadline (48 hrs)|Anyone can comment|Decision maker decides after deadline|Document decision + reasoning
Avoid_This: Consensus (everyone must agree)|No deadline (decision limbo)|Decision without documentation|Reopening decided issues without new data

Description: Remote onboarding needs MORE structure than in-person. Day 1 buddy + Week 1 checklist + 30-60-90 plan + daily check-ins for first 2 weeks.
Why_It_Matters: New remote hire's first 2 weeks determine their success trajectory. Poor onboarding = quiet quit within 3 months.
Do_This: Day 1: can access everything + ship something small|Assign onboarding buddy (same timezone if possible)|Daily 15-min check-in for week 1|Week 1: first meaningful contribution|Recorded Loom walkthroughs for common questions
Avoid_This: 'Figure it out' approach|No buddy|Information dump on day 1|No check-ins|Expecting productivity in week 1
